title: The Power of Absence: Thinking with Archival Theory in Algorithmic Design

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative evaluation through design speculation analyzing AI language translation tools (e.g., Google Translate) to reveal hidden gendered assumptions when translating gender-neutral English phrases into languages with gendered structures like Japanese.

Qualitative evaluation through design speculation that exposes ageist assumptions embedded in translation algorithms regarding the presumed age, seniority, and societal roles of speakers and listeners.

Theoretical and qualitative evaluation using critical archival theory, Black feminist thought, and generative AI design speculations (e.g., reimagining urban architecture with Black quilting traditions) to highlight the systemic omission of Black cultural production and knowledge from computational datasets.

Artistic experimentation that involves processing non-standard, spiritual speech ('glossolalia' or speaking in tongues) through machine translation algorithms to demonstrate the limitations of AI in recognizing complex, localized, or unmapped linguistic phenomena.
